question: Should OpenClaw add a native child-session context-pressure notification and recovery contract, and if so should it be diagnostics-only, parent-routed, or operator-actionable?
rationale: Current code has context usage data but no established product contract for thresholds, parent identity, alert destinations, or automatic recovery, and VISION.md cautions against default agent-hierarchy frameworks.

options.title: Define a narrow session-health contract
options.body: Add context-pressure detection to diagnostics/session health, surface it to parent/operator paths, and keep recovery bounded and explicitly configured.

options.title: Telemetry-only for now
options.body: Let the diagnostics telemetry work land first and defer parent notification until maintainers have live fleet proof and a cleaner recovery design.

options.title: Decline parent orchestration
options.body: Treat parent notification and recovery routing as external orchestration policy unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow session-health contract
recommendation.body: Add context-pressure detection to diagnostics/session health, surface it to parent/operator paths, and keep recovery bounded and explicitly configured.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses VISION.md product scope, session-state behavior, and the agent-hierarchy guardrail, making the product-routing owner the safest decision point.
